title: Islamic Bank Shariah Review Operations
thesis: Snowflake turns daily Shariah review activity from a fictional Malaysian Islamic bank into clean review rate and documentation exception KPIs, 7-day escalation risk scores, document rejection anomalies and grounded AI answers, all on curated dynamic tables.

talking_points: Clean review rate, documentation exceptions, escalations to the Shariah committee and the MYR value of contracts reviewed for 40 financing portfolios in Kuala Lumpur, George Town, Johor Bahru, Kota Kinabalu and Kuching.
The portfolios cover tawarruq personal financing, murabahah SME financing, musharakah mutanaqisah home financing, ijarah vehicle financing and wakalah trade financing.
Every KPI is a numerator over a denominator in a curated dynamic table, so it can be traced back to portfolio-day rows.
The exception-reason chart shows which reasons end in escalation and which are always rectified, such as document system outages.
tabs.call_out: One governed set of Shariah review KPIs, traceable to source rows

transition.line: Which portfolios should the review team watch first?

talking_points: Snowflake ML classification scores each portfolio's probability of an exception escalated to the Shariah committee in the next 7 days.
The holdout line shows precision and recall on the most recent labelled days, against the base rate.
Anomaly detection flags document rejection rate outliers per portfolio, and the forecast projects bank-wide exception volume for 14 days.
tabs.call_out: Honest, evaluated ML inside the data platform

transition.line: Are our process controls keeping up?

talking_points: Branch process review compliance, contract file coverage and pending documents frame the control gaps.
Process review compliance against escalated exceptions by portfolio shows where missed reviews and escalations move together; it is an association, not proof of cause.
The action memo drafts three prioritised operational actions from the KPI, portfolio, exception-reason and risk tables only.
show: Process review compliance and file coverage
Process review compliance vs escalated exceptions
tabs.call_out: Grounded draft actions, with a human in the loop

transition.line: What happens when a review finds an exception right now?

talking_points: Live review result events land in RAW.LIVE_REVIEWS, from the simulator or from Amazon Data Firehose through Snowpipe.
The Snowflake alert logs EXCEPTION results with an SOP hint and the portfolio's current risk band, then emails the on-duty Shariah review officer.
tabs.call_out: From review exception to follow-up in one platform

talking_points: The Cortex Agent uses Cortex Analyst over the semantic view for metrics, and Cortex Search over 13 synthetic exception-handling SOPs.

Each answer shows the generated SQL and the SOPs it cited. The SOPs are operational only; escalated matters are decided by the bank's Shariah committee, and the demo makes no Shariah, religious or regulatory rulings.

transition.line: Here is how it is built.

talking_points: Two builds share one core: Snowflake only, or AWS + Snowflake (Data Firehose, Bedrock, QuickSight and Amazon Q).
Everything shown is synthetic demo data, rebuilt reproducibly from the repo.
tabs.call_out: One governed core, with an optional AWS edge
